clue.text: Plant coming from Japan, a singular rich source

parts.note: J is the abbreviation for Japan (its international vehicle code)
S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular
a mine is a rich source, as in 'a mine of information'

explanation.surface: A botanist notes that a certain plant comes from Japan and is uniquely abundant there.
explanation.definitionFit: Jasmine is a fragrant climbing shrub, so it is a kind of plant.

clue.text: Nervous youth's beginning to represent craze in dance

indicators.note: to represent means one letter stands in place of another word in the dance

parts.note: the jitterbug is an energetic swing dance
a bug is a craze or enthusiasm, as in 'the travel bug'

indicators.note: beginning means the first letter of youth's

explanation.surface: An anxious teenager's first attempt to express a dance craze.
explanation.walkthrough: BUG (craze) in JITTERBUG is replaced by Y, the first letter of youth's.
explanation.definitionFit: Jittery is a synonym for anxious or on edge.

clue.text: Feature of cricket day in a tie?

parts.note: the square is the central area of a cricket ground where pitches are laid

explanation.surface: A question whether a feature of a cricket day is a match ending level.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the square is the closely mown central strip of the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A contest that is squared is level, the scores being all square, as in a tie.

clue.text: Urge shown by politician bound by dreadful lie

indicators.note: bound by means enclosed by, so one piece sits within the other
dreadful suggests something badly done, so the letters of lie are jumbled

parts.note: MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A pressure applied by a member of parliament caught in a terrible falsehood.
explanation.definitionFit: To impel is to drive or push someone to act, a synonym for urge.

clue.text: Nice person's expression of confidence?

parts.note: Nice seems to mean pleasant but is the French city, so a French speaker's phrase for something said in secret

explanation.surface: A kindly person's way of showing self-assurance.
explanation.walkthrough: Nice, capitalised, is the French Riviera city; the misleading reading is a nice, pleasant person.
explanation.definitionFit: This French phrase meaning between ourselves is used to introduce something said in confidence.

clue.text: Ornamental boat boarded by Oscar

indicators.note: a boat boarded by someone has them inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a barque is a sailing ship
Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A decorated vessel has a passenger called Oscar climbing aboard.
explanation.definitionFit: Baroque describes the highly decorated, elaborate style of seventeenth-century art and architecture.

clue.text: Book linked to ultimate thrilling experience

parts.note: ultimate means final or last

explanation.surface: A novel tied to the ultimate in excitement.
explanation.definitionFit: A blast is informal for a very enjoyable time, as in 'the party was a blast'.

clue.text: Disown celebrity accepting help in need of lift

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: repute means fame or celebrity

indicators.note: in a down clue a lift raises the word, so help is read from bottom to top

parts.note: aid means help

explanation.surface: Renounce a famous person who has accepted help while needing a boost.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, 'in need of lift' means the word for help is read upwards; 'celebrity' is fame here, not a famous person.
explanation.definitionFit: To repudiate is to reject or refuse to acknowledge, a synonym for disown.

clue.text: Barney Fletcher's trademark?

definitions.meaning: barney is British slang for a noisy row or argument
a fletcher makes arrows, and a crossbow bolt bears this name

explanation.surface: A man named Barney is asked about Fletcher's brand name.
explanation.walkthrough: Barney and Fletcher look like names; barney is slang for a row, and a fletcher is an arrow-maker.
explanation.definitionFit: A row is an argument, and a short square-headed crossbow bolt is also called by this word.

clue.text: Like an ancient tree close to school yard

parts.note: the elder is a small tree with white flowers and dark berries

indicators.note: close means end, so close to school is that word's last letter

explanation.surface: An old tree stands near a playground beside a school.
explanation.definitionFit: Elderly means old, so describes something that resembles an aged person.

clue.text: Drink in time cherished? It's good for a blast

indicators.note: the drink is placed inside the combined time-and-cherished letters

parts.note: a pet is someone cherished, a favourite
rum is an alcoholic drink

explanation.surface: Someone praises a spell of drinking with a loved one as good for a blowout.
explanation.definitionFit: A trumpet is a brass instrument that produces a loud blast of sound when blown.

clue.text: Give a hand to a lad with pup that's unruly

indicators.note: unruly suggests disorder, so the letters of the preceding words are jumbled

explanation.surface: Praise a boy who owns a badly behaved puppy.
explanation.definitionFit: To give someone a hand is an idiom for clapping them, which is to applaud.

clue.text: Loner unusually for audience planned record

indicators.note: unusually signals that the letters of loner are set out in an unusual order
something for an audience is heard rather than read, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: meant means intended or planned

explanation.surface: A solitary person, out of character, arranges a recorded event in front of spectators.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusually' rearranges LONER to ENROL; 'for audience' turns MEANT (planned) into its sound-alike MENT.
explanation.definitionFit: An enrolment is an entry on a register, so it serves as a record of membership.

clue.text: Artist about to enter reception without counter

indicators.note: to enter means to go inside, so one piece sits within the other
without means lacking, so the following letters are taken away

parts.note: a durbar is a formal reception held by an Indian prince or colonial ruler
a bar is a counter where drinks are served
re is a common word meaning about or concerning

explanation.surface: A painter arrives at a function to find there is no service desk.
explanation.walkthrough: A durbar was a ceremonial reception at an Indian prince's court; 'counter' is a bar, not someone who counts.
explanation.definitionFit: Albrecht Dürer was a German Renaissance painter and engraver.

clue.text: Effect of Swiss air?

parts.note: air seems to mean the mountain atmosphere but is a tune; a characteristic Swiss song is the warbling Alpine call

explanation.surface: A question about what the bracing Alpine climate does to a person.
explanation.definitionFit: The warbling song of Alpine herdsmen, switching between chest voice and falsetto, is a Swiss air.

clue.text: Dog disrupting a shop alas

indicators.note: disrupting means throwing into disorder, so the following letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A hound causes havoc in a store, much to everyone's dismay.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lhasa apso is a small long-haired breed originally from Tibet.

clue.text: Grey part of castle in which some are heard?

parts.note: grey-haired, hence old
the bailey is the outer courtyard of a castle

explanation.surface: A weathered section of fortress where some voices echo.
explanation.walkthrough: The Old Bailey is London's Central Criminal Court, where cases are heard.
explanation.definitionFit: Court cases are heard at this London criminal court, so it is a place where some cases are tried.

clue.text: One engaged in argument abstracted around bar largely

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: abstracted means distracted or distant

explanation.walkthrough: 'largely' drops the last letter of the word for bar; 'abstracted' means absent-minded, not removed.
explanation.definitionFit: A disputant is a person taking part in a dispute or debate.

clue.text: Creative site producing standard animal in Norway and America

parts.note: par is a standard or norm

indicators.note: the animal sits inside the combined country letters

parts.note: N is the international vehicle code for Norway
US is short for the United States of America
an ass is a donkey

explanation.surface: An artistic venue turns out a typical beast found in Scandinavia and the USA.
explanation.definitionFit: Mount Parnassus was sacred to Apollo and the Muses, so it stands for the home of poetry and creativity.

clue.text: I almost forgot about gallery with very good artist

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece sits around the other

parts.note: PS, a postscript, is what you add when you almost forgot something
the ICA is the Institute of Contemporary Arts, a London gallery
so means very, as in 'so kind'

explanation.surface: Someone nearly forgets to mention a gallery that holds work by a fine painter.
explanation.walkthrough: The ICA is the Institute of Contemporary Arts in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Pablo Picasso was a Spanish painter, among the most celebrated artists of the twentieth century.

clue.text: Substitute starts to exercise pretty loosely in contest

indicators.note: in signals that these letters go inside the contest

indicators.note: starts to means the first letters of the following words

explanation.surface: A reserve player starts some casual exercise during a match.
explanation.definitionFit: To replace is to put something in another's place, synonymous with substitute as a verb.

clue.text: Creator of bars having brewed lager

clue.text: Taste not wholly associated with a revolutionary painting

explanation.definitionFit: Gouache is opaque watercolour paint, and a picture painted in it.

clue.text: Illegal profit for fake rogue

explanation.surface: Crooked gains are made by a con man faking it.

clue.text: It could be finished quietly in café? Not half

definitions.text: It could be finished quietly in café? Not half

indicators.note: the finished and quiet letters go inside the café part
not half keeps only one half of the word café

parts.note: up means over or finished, as in 'time's up'
p (piano) is the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: Something might be drunk up softly in a coffee shop, though only partly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half' keeps the first half of café. Read whole, the clue also describes the drink itself, finished in a café.
explanation.definitionFit: A cuppa is a British colloquial cup of tea, the sort of thing finished off in a café.

clue.text: Singer curtailed performance in front of King, rebellious type?

indicators.note: in front of places the singer before the following pieces

parts.note: Neil Young is a singer-songwriter

parts.note: a turn is a stage act or performance

explanation.surface: A vocalist cuts short his act before a monarch, asking whether he is a rebel.

clue.text: Agreement given about advertising battle site

clue.text: A sailor docked with company touring island and island capital

clue.text: One taking drink tucking into crumbly feta

explanation.walkthrough: 'crumbly' rearranges feta and 'tucking into' sets the beer inside. Tea leaf is Cockney rhyming slang for thief.
